replying_to: Replying to Adaptive Unbiased Teacher for Cross-Domain Object Detection
display_title: Official Review of Paper973 by Reviewer 6y7a

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors tackle the problem of cross-domain object detection using a teacher-student mechanism with adversarial learning and weak-strong data augmentation. The teacher network is trained on the target domain, while the student learns from both domains. In this way, the teacher improves without suffering domain shift. The adversarial setup ensures that the distributions from the source and target domains are aligned in the student network.
content.main_review:
The paper addresses an interesting, yet difficult problem for which the current approaches do not perform very well. 

The paper is pretty well written, with the method clearly explained, although I feel that more details about the detailed related work should have been added.

The results look promising, with tables showing that the proposed method achieves the best performance in multiple scenarios. Still, the evaluation seems to be lacking a key element: even if multiple papers have the same base model, they can learn better or worse depending on multiple elements. The absolute gain is a more reliable method than mAP evaluation, and results should be reported considering the base model of each paper. 

Furthermore, I believe that the ablation study should be extended, providing the results of multiple combinations of the existing components. 

It would also be interesting to see what happens when using a different object detector?
content.summary_of_the_review:
I believe that the paper tackles an interesting problem and shows good results. Still, I think the evaluation section and the ablation study should be enhanced. The paper is not highly novel, most works in this area being based on the same ideas. As the authors note, teacher-student networks and pseudo-labels have already been successfully employed in cross-domain object detection tasks. Still, some relevant papers have not been added at all in the related work section, e.g. [A].

I think these problems should be addressed before the paper can be accepted at such a high quality venue.

[A] Soviany et al. Curriculum self-paced learning for cross-domain object detection. Computer Vision and Image Understanding, 204, p.103166, 2021.

replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper973 by Reviewer 6y7a

content.title: Response to reviewer 6y7a
content.comment:
We thank the reviewer for their thoughtful review. We address their main concerns below.

**Re: the evaluation seems to be lacking a key element: even if multiple papers have the same base model, they can learn better or worse depending on multiple elements. The absolute gain is a more reliable method than mAP evaluation, and results should be reported considering the base model of each paper.**


As stated in the paper, our model leverages the Mean Teacher and weak-strong augmentation. To make a fair comparison, the network is evaluated and compared with other models with the same base model, e.g., we only used Faster RCNN and the same backbones following previous works while other competitors may introduce additional more elements on that. On the other hand, Table 4 shows the performance gain given by each element. In general, our experiments basically unveiled that Mean Teacher or Unbiased Teacher will benefit from adversarial learning which is the key point in our model.

**Re: Furthermore, I believe that the ablation study should be extended, providing the results of multiple combinations of the existing components.**

For the existing components, we refer to the Mean Teacher, adversarial learning, and augmentation. We do provide such ablation studies in Table 4. Though these modules are from the existing methods in computer vision society, we are among the first to leverage Mean Teacher with adversarial learning properly and address our raised issue regarding pseudo labeling successfully.


**Re: It would also be interesting to see what happens when using a different object detector?**

We thank the reviewer for noting that different detectors are worth trying to see the effectiveness. On the other hand, we used Faster RCNN for fair comparison and evaluated our proposed model easily though it is worth trying different detectors. We will provide more experiments using other detectors. 

**Re: Some relevant papers have not been added at all in the related work section, e.g. [A].
[A] Soviany et al. Curriculum self-paced learning for cross-domain object detection. Computer Vision and Image Understanding, 204, p.103166, 2021.**

We thank the reviewer for noting the missing citations regarding cross-domain object detection. We will refine the related works accordingly.

content.title: Replay to rebuttal
content.comment: After reading the rebuttal and the paper (again), I realised that the authors "do not apply unsupervised losses for the bounding box regression" on the target domain, which I think is not fair for the baseline. I think this choice pretty much explains why the proposed method surpasses the oracles. To this end, the method is no longer seen as doing unsupervised domain adaptation. Also, the authors did not address the novelty concern. As such, I decided to keep my score unchanged.

content.title: Re: Replay to rebuttal
content.comment: We are sorry that we did not make this clear thus the reviewer does not understand the point. ''do not apply unsupervised losses for the bounding box regression'' means we do not apply regression loss of the bounding box from the pseudo labels but only apply class loss to train the model. We are always following the setting of unsupervised domain adaptation (labeled source domain and unlabeled target domain).

replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper973 by Reviewer Pqep

content.title: Response to Reviewer Pqep
content.comment:
We thank the reviewer for their thoughtful review. We address their main concerns below.

**Re: It looks like one target domain for one discriminator? Is it possible to use a conditional discriminator for model-compact purposes?**

We thank the reviewer for providing us with this potential extension of our model to use a conditional discriminator for model-compact purposes. We will extend our model by including this useful and application idea if possible in the future. Currently, we only have tried one target domain to follow the general setting of domain adaptation (one source domain and one target domain).

**Re: Any ablation study for the choice of confidence threshold?**

We thank the reviewer for the request. We select 0.8 as the threshold for simplicity and stability. We will provide the analysis on this in the future as the edited supplementary. A preliminary study on both thresholding \delta and \lambda_unsup can be provided as follows on the Clipart1k dataset. We sweep the thresholding through 0.6 to 0.9. The experiment shows that setting thresholding with \delta=0.8 achieves the best result though this parameter could lead to only a slight difference.

| Ablation studies on \lambda_unsup and \delta  |             |              |              |              |              |              |              |
|-------------------|--------------|--------------|--------------|--------------|--------------|--------------|--------------|
|\lambda_unsup=1.0  |
| lr = 0.06         |              |              |              | lr = 0.04    |              |              |              |
| \delta = 0.6      | \delta = 0.7 | \delta = 0.8 | \delta = 0.9 | \delta = 0.6 | \delta = 0.7 | \delta = 0.8 | \delta = 0.9 |
| 48.57             | 47.97        | 49.18        | 48.15        | 47.53        | 47.14        | 49.08        | 49.01        |
| \lambda_unsup=2.0 |              |              |              |              |              |              |              |
| 45.5              | 45.73        | 47.4         | 47.21        | 47.23        | 46.8         | 50.01        | 48.67        |

**Re: Some questions about the implementation details. Any reason to set \lambda_unsup as 1, equivalent for labeled and unlabeled data. Because for unbiased teacher paper, they have larger weight for unsupervised loss.**

We set \lambda_unsup as 1 is just for simple implementation. The preliminary ablation studies are shown above. We will provide further with this parameter analysis into supplementary material. 

**Re: Why use different backbones for two domain adaptations. Real to Artistic Adaptation for resnet-101 but Weather Adaptation or VGG16?**

We thank the reviewer for noting the ambiguity. We chose different backbones just for fair comparisons with state-of-the-art approaches. Each set has its own used benchmark backbones as we follow the previous works.

**Re: Any insights to explain why for some specific classes, the performances of the proposed methods are worse than other methods? For example, aero, bicycle, bus, dogs, etc. Although the averaged mAP is the best, 7/20 are worse, not a small ratio.**


We thank the reviewer for raising the insightful question. We are still analyzing the problem with suboptimal performance on some classes on Clipart. However, our model achieves the best or comparable results on each class of other datasets.

**Re: I think the results of the original unbiased teacher should be added in Tables 1 and 3. Because this is a strong baseline.**

We thank the reviewer for noting the original unbiased teacher (UT) can be added for comparison. Actually, UT can be seen as the model in Table 4 (the one AUT w/o \mathcal{L}_{dis}) which is used without adversarial loss.

**Re: Similar to the ablation study on weak augmentation, one curiosity is if the strong augmentation does matter. For example, will the performance changes a lot when adding or eliminating more strong augmentation for the current sets, like those in AutoAugment?**

We thank the reviewer for noting the importance of strong augmentation. If referred to Table 4, we can observe that model without strong augmentation will lead to a performance drop. We can add more analysis on changing the types of strong augmentations

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes Adaptive Unbiased Teacher for cross-domain object detection. The proposed method integrates teacher-student learning with gradient reverse layer as well as adversarial learning, and obtains good improvement on adapting object detector on Clipart1K, Watercolor2K and Foggy Cityscape datasets.
content.main_review:
It is not very easy to read and understand this paper. First, a number of terms were given without explanation; Second, the proposed system has multiple components and I am not sure about the overall novelty. In addition, it is not clear how easy it is to adjust the weights across multiple components. 

In more details:
- Figure 1: what does "mean teacher" mean?
- Section 3.1, para 2: what is "weakly augmented" and what is "strongly augmented"? Note that Figure 1 also mentioned "Weak-Strong" augmentation, and I am not very sure about these meanings.
- Section 3.2, eq(1): better explain what "L_cls" and "L_reg" mean. 
- Section 3.2, eq(2): could you explain why this equation can reduce the amount of false alarms?
- Section 3.2, eq(3): does this update happen in every SGD step after every batch? Or update after every epoch?
- Section 4: could you show the evolvement of curves during training (different loss, detection rate on source & target dataset)?
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper proposes a reasonable method with good performance improvement.  It is not clear whether the proposed method is easy to use or not, and the presentation of the paper could be improved.

replying_to: Replying to Official Review of Paper973 by Reviewer QLcT

content.title: Response to Reviewer QLcT
content.comment:
We thank the reviewer for their thoughtful review. We address their main concerns below.

**Re: Figure 1: what does "mean teacher" mean?**

We thank the reviewer for noting this ambiguity in Figure 1. “Mean teacher” refers to the previously proposed model which we have cited in the paper. We will add the additional citation in the caption. 

**Re: Section 3.1, para 2: what is "weakly augmented" and what is "strongly augmented"? Note that Figure 1 also mentioned "Weak-Strong" augmentation, and I am not very sure about these meanings.**

We thank the reviewer for pointing out the ambiguity for naming. These naming can be referred to Section 3.2 where we stated that: “the target samples are augmented with random horizontal flip and crop for weak augmentation in Teacher model and randomly color jittering,  grayscale,  Gaussian blur,  and cutout patches for strong augmentations as perturbations.”  Weak-Strong means weakly augmentation as input of the Teacher to provide reliable pseudo-labels while images with strong augmentation as inputs of the Student. We will emphasize more about this abbreviation in the caption.

**Re: Section 3.2, eq(1): better explain what "L_cls" and "L_reg" mean.**

We thank the reviewer for noting this ambiguity. "L_cls" and "L_reg" indicate the classification and regression loss used in Faster RCNN. We also mentioned in the paper that these are referred to as bounding box regression (reg) and classification (cls).

**Re: Section 3.2, eq(2): could you explain why this equation can reduce the amount of false alarms?**

We thank the reviewer for noting this ambiguity. As stated in the section explaining eq(2), “we set a confidence threshold of predicted bounding boxes to filter predicted bounding boxes of low-confidence, which are possibly the false positive samples”. That is, thresholding the confidence can reduce the number of false alarms here.

**Re: Section 3.2, eq(3): does this update happen in every SGD step after every batch? Or update after every epoch?**

We thank the reviewer for noting this ambiguity. Yes, we update every step after every batch same as other used losses.

**Re: Section 4: could you show the evolvement of curves during training (different loss, detection rate on source & target dataset)?**

We thank the reviewer for the request. While we have those documents generated in tensorboard, we did not include them in the main paper due to the space. We will provide them in the edited supplementary materi
